Really beautiful trail.    I listened to many podcasts (GGB) and took my new barefoot shoes for a trek.  I loved seeing so many families by the river as the sun was setting.  Lots of terrain but I never felt exhausted.  I loved how curiosity provoking it was.    I saw a beaver for the first time outside of the zoo in action.   I showed a man and his father and they later on the trail showed me how to identify the trees that the beavers were chopping down.   So cool ! I wish I lived nearby to see if the beaver completes his task.   Lots of birds (Merlin app is great to help identify if you’re interested).   I felt safe walking alone.  I loved that there wasn’t loud car sounds or garbage like the trails in Toronto.   Many people fishing.  A few new bridges  being made.   Loved the plaques with moments to pause and reflect on what to be thankful for with artwork by Rick Hill.     I was feeling spiritually weary and this walk lifted me up.

One of our favourite local trails! The pup loved this too. It’s no wonder it’s rated so highly on here. It has a bit of everything - serene wooded paths through the forest, a beautiful viewpoint of the creek from above, private areas by the water to skip rocks, tall shrubs, picturesque bridges, paved trails and rocky & terrain trails for those who like a challenge. It’s quite leisurely, although there are many uphill portions, but they are all pretty easy and doable. The vistas and panoramas of the forest are magnificent for something so close to the city. It is also not crowded during peak summer times. There are other people around, but few and far between. The majority of the trail is yours to explore and discover in private and alone - except for the amazing wildlife. There are many different parts of the trail to do and I believe it extends over 30km, if not much longer. We’ve done about half of that with the puppy and thoroughly enjoyed it. It’s great for cyclists as well. On a side note, the best place to park is through the cultural centre and then walk down the paved path until you see a dirt path on the left. Take that dirt path up to the better part of the trail (in our opinion). Then follow directions for the West Bank trail, and come back around to the East Bank trail - about 15km.

I only walk 1/3 the distance today to test out the trail condition to see if this trail is good for 1) taking a large group of people to walk all 6 km; 2) check to see if there is a good spot to fly my drone.  Answer for #1 is yes, easy walk, some shade, mostly flat level with some steps. Perfect for a group with different level of hiking experience.  But not really too much scenery.  Answer to #2 is no, there hardly any good place to fly drone.  The creek is fairly small and narrow.  Very limited space you can fly to see.
